meta.description: Physical Talents (Körperliche Talente) from TDE 4.1. These talents involve physical actions where encumbrance plays a major role. Most are column D; some easier ones are column C. Both open and contested tests are possible, and some may be rolled secretly by the Highlord.

talents.name: Acrobatics
talents.description: This talent covers everything a mountebank trains for: balancing, swinging on ropes and trapezes, cartwheeling, and death-defying somersaults. Whenever a hero wants to perform an action worthy of a circus artist — all willfully executed acrobatic actions — an Acrobatics test may be called for. Less spectacular feats of body control, such as rolling after a fall from a horse, fall under the Body Control talent instead. Requires Body Control 4 to attempt any tests.

talents.name: Athletics
talents.description: The ability to focus Strength, Agility, and Constitution into one action and excel at classical athletic events — rarely to win a laurel wreath in a competition, but usually because running long distances or lifting heavy loads is part of the profession. Athletics is the active use of physical abilities (as opposed to Body Control, which applies to reactions to external events). Tests can increase sprinting speed, reduce endurance loss when running long distances, support a Strength test for lifting, or increase maximum jump height and distance.

talents.name: Body Control
talents.description: Slipping on a steep staircase, rolling after a fall from a horse, a diving leap over a collapsing bridge section, or staying on one's feet on a ship in a storm — in all these cases Body Control is required. The more difficult the situation, the higher the difficulty increase. Acrobatics requires Body Control 4. Rules for falling and fall damage are in the combat chapter.

talents.name: Carouse
talents.description: A hero can be invited to a feast that brings them to their limits at any time. Usually heavy drinking leads to gains in Courage and reductions of certain fears, but drastic penalties on all other good attributes, as well as increases in attributes like Curiosity, Superstition, and especially Violent Temper. Successful Carouse tests can negate these effects. A successful Carouse test also wards off the usual morning-after hangover — in Aventuria called 'Wolf' or 'Werewolf' depending on severity.

talents.name: Climb
talents.description: A Climb test is required whenever the hero undertakes a difficult climb — such as scaling a castle wall or a sheer cliff. Depending on the type and height of the obstacle, difficulty increases may apply; well-used climbing aids (pitons, ropes, grappling hooks) naturally make the test easier. A hero with the Vertigo disadvantage rolls additional Vertigo tests or their climb tests are increased by the Vertigo value. Since one can fall while climbing, see the rules for falling and fall damage.

talents.name: Dance
talents.description: Successful Dance tests can bring great advantages not only at a count's court but also at a witch's feast, while a failed test can expose even the most impressive hero to ridicule and cost them social prestige. This talent governs basic coordination of movement and a feel for rhythm; for complicated courtly dances, a solid knowledge of Etiquette is also needed; for dances from foreign cultures, also the Kulturkunde special ability.

talents.name: Hide
talents.description: This talent determines the ability to quickly find a suitable hiding spot and use it. A hero whose talent test fails has either underestimated the Perception of their pursuers or was too indecisive. In an environment offering absolutely no hiding spots, the Highlord need not allow a test. Tests may be rolled secretly by the Highlord; a Contested Test against Perception is also possible.

talents.name: Juggling
talents.description: Covers all the little tricks a mountebank can use to earn money at a fair or possibly save their life as a prisoner of unscrupulous bandits: juggling, ventriloquism, fire-eating, etc. So-called 'side interests' like shell games also fall under this talent, but not cheating with cards and dice (see the Cheat talent).

talents.name: Perception
talents.description: Whenever a hero wants to gain information related to the five senses, a Perception test is in order. Applies to smelling fragrances as well as spotting distant targets, to identifying poisoned wine by taste as well as tracing filigreed engravings by touch. Tests involving hearing, tasting, or smelling are rolled against CL/IN/IN; those involving tactile sense use CL/IN/DE instead. All tests should be rolled in secret by the Highlord. A failed test means the hero notices nothing or receives incorrect information. EEC varies by situation up to EC.

talents.name: Pick Pockets
talents.description: Whether cutting purses or stealing unnoticed from a stranger's shoulder bag — many heroes of not entirely spotless reputation employ this talent. Factors affecting difficulty: does the victim suspect a theft? How bulky is the loot? Does the thief have an accomplice who bumps into the victim or distracts in another way? An attempted theft can be countered by a successful Perception test. Requires Human Nature 4 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Ride
talents.description: A hero does not need this talent just to stay on a horse walking and being led by someone else. However, they will not be able to make the horse go in a specific direction when the animal has other ideas. Tests become necessary for extraordinary performances: hard gallop and jumps over obstacles (even low ones) require tests; rides across rough terrain and riding without reins also require tests with difficulty increases. Ride tests are also used for flying creatures like pterosaurs or hippogriffs (automatic +5 difficulty for those not usually mounted on such creatures).

talents.name: Willpower
talents.description: Willpower encompasses the ability to withstand great pain. High TP is useful not only on the torture rack but also in combat (to avoid losing consciousness after a heavy hit) or on a grueling forced march. Willpower is also required when resisting temptations or suppressing a laugh or a taunting remark. In some situations, a Violent Temper or Pride test may be more appropriate — or those values may be imposed as difficulty increases on the Willpower test.

talents.name: Sing
talents.description: Although not everyone is blessed with a beautiful singing voice, it can be developed and trained. The Sing talent is suitable for solo singing, reciting a heroic epic, or accompanying music — a decent performance is expected of novices in certain cults as well as professional singers, bards, and skalds.

talents.name: Sneak
talents.description: Successful sneaking depends not only on body control but also on attentiveness — to recognize potential noise sources like creaking floorboards or dry twigs on the ground and avoid them. The terrain and the hero's clothing also play an important role. Difficulty increases depend on terrain, armor, and footwear. A Sneak test can be countered by a successful Perception test. The Highlord should roll the hero's tests in secret.

talents.name: Swim
talents.description: A hero with TP 2 can tread water and move slowly in the desired direction — they need not roll a test when falling into a small pond. Tests are required when the hero wants to perform an extraordinary action in water: diving, carrying an encumbering load, pulling a companion, or fighting. Factors affecting difficulty: current (raging breakers or a mountain torrent can cause up to +8), and the hero's armor. Distance covered while swimming depends on Endurance.

talents.name: Voice Mimicry
talents.description: A good TP in this talent primarily indicates the ability to convincingly imitate animal voices; at higher talent values it is possible to imitate human voices. In both cases, the imitator must have had sufficient opportunity to study the specific sound and practice it. Only a master imitator with TP of at least 15 can, for example, answer on behalf of a Minister of State with his master's voice on the first attempt. Requires Perception 4.
